purpose: cjson is a lightweight C library for parsing and generating JSON.

functions.cJSON_AddFalseToObject: `cJSON_AddFalseToObject` creates a JSON `false` item and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it for object members only. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL` (e.g., bad object/name or add failure).
functions.cJSON_CreateNumber: `cJSON_CreateNumber` creates a new JSON number item. Use it to build a `cJSON_Number` node from a `double`. It sets `valuedouble` to `num` and `valueint` with saturation: `INT_MAX`/`INT_MIN` on overflow, otherwise `(int)num`. Returns `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToObject: Adds `item` to `object` under `string` as a **reference** (not a deep copy). Use it when you want multiple JSON nodes to share the same value. Returns `false` if `object` or `string` is `NULL`; otherwise delegates to `create_reference(item, ...)` and insertion.
functions.cJSON_CreateBool: `cJSON_CreateBool` creates a new JSON boolean item. Pass a `cJSON_bool`; nonzero becomes `cJSON_True`, zero becomes `cJSON_False`. It allocates a new `cJSON` node via `cJSON_New_Item(&global_hooks)` and returns it, or `NULL` if allocation fails.
functions.cJSON_AddRawToObject: `cJSON_AddRawToObject` creates a raw JSON item from `raw` and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it when you want to insert preformatted JSON text as-is. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithOpts: Parses JSON from a C string. Use it when you want to optionally require a trailing `\0` and/or get the parse end pointer. Returns `NULL` on `NULL` input or parse error; on failure `return_parse_end` points to the error location.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLength: `cJSON_ParseWithLength` is a convenience wrapper for parsing JSON from a non-null-terminated buffer of known length. Use it when the input may contain extra data past `buffer_length` or isn’t NUL-terminated. It just calls `cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts(..., 0, 0)`.
functions.cJSON_Version: `cJSON_Version()` returns a static, null-terminated string with the library version in `major.minor.patch` form. Call it with no args; it formats the version into an internal buffer and returns that pointer. Repeated calls overwrite the same buffer.
functions.cJSON_Delete: Deletes a cJSON node and its descendants. Use it to free a parsed/created tree. It walks `next` siblings, recursively deletes `child`, and frees `valuestring`/`string` unless marked `cJSON_IsReference` or `cJSON_StringIsConst`.
functions.cJSON_Duplicate: `cJSON_Duplicate` makes a copy of a `cJSON` item. Use it on an existing node; set `recurse` true to deep-copy children, false to copy only the item itself. If `item` is `NULL`, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsInvalid: `cJSON_IsInvalid` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the `cJSON_Invalid` type. Use it to test an item before handling it as a valid JSON value. It returns `false` for `NULL`; otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Invalid`.
functions.cJSON_malloc: `cJSON_malloc` is a thin wrapper around the allocator set by `cJSON_InitHooks`. Use it when you need cJSON’s configured heap behavior. It simply calls `global_hooks.allocate(size)` and returns that result, so it follows the active custom/default malloc semantics.
functions.cJSON_IsArray: `cJSON_IsArray` checks whether a `cJSON*` points to a JSON array. Use it on an item pointer; it returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Array`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObjectCS: Adds `item` to `object` under a const key string. Use only when `string` is guaranteed to outlive the cJSON object. It marks the key as const, so cJSON won’t free it; don’t modify `item->string` unless `cJSON_StringIsConst` is clear.
functions.cJSON_GetStringValue: `cJSON_GetStringValue` is a safe accessor for a JSON string item’s `valuestring`. Use it only on `cJSON` nodes that should be strings. It returns the stored `char*` when `cJSON_IsString(item)` is true; otherwise it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateFalse: `cJSON_CreateFalse()` creates a new cJSON value representing JSON `false`. Use it when building a JSON tree and you need a boolean false node. It allocates a new item; on allocation failure it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateTrue: `cJSON_CreateTrue` creates a new cJSON boolean node set to JSON `true`. Use it when building JSON trees programmatically. It allocates a new item with `cJSON_New_Item`; if allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromArray: Detaches the item at index `which` from a cJSON array and returns it without deleting it. Use with `which >= 0`; negative returns `NULL`. If the index is out of range, the helper returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateObjectReference: Creates a new cJSON object/array node that *references* an existing child list. Use it when you want `cJSON_Delete` to free only the wrapper, not the referenced elements. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject: `cJSON_DeleteItemFromObject` removes an item from a JSON object by key and then frees it. Use it on an object node with the target name. If the key isn’t found, nothing is deleted; if found, the item is detached and deleted.
functions.cJSON_IsNumber: `cJSON_IsNumber` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a number node. Use it on a non-NULL `cJSON*` before reading numeric fields. It returns `false` for `NULL` or any non-number type, otherwise `true`.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItem: `cJSON_GetObjectItem` retrieves a named child from a JSON object using a case-insensitive key match. Pass an object node and the key string; it returns the matching `cJSON*` or `NULL` if the object/key is invalid or no match exists.
functions.cJSON_IsObject: `cJSON_IsObject` checks whether a `cJSON*` points to a JSON object. Use it before treating `item` as an object. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-object type; `true` only when `item->type & 0xFF == cJSON_Object`.
functions.cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive: `cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive` looks up a child item in a JSON object by key using exact case matching. Use it with a `cJSON` object and key string. It returns the matching `cJSON*` if found, otherwise `NULL`; it doesn’t modify the object.
functions.cJSON_Parse: `cJSON_Parse` is a simple wrapper for `cJSON_ParseWithOpts(value, 0, 0)`. It parses a JSON string into a `cJSON*` tree. On success, free it with `cJSON_Delete`; on failure, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInArray: Replaces the item at index `which` in a cJSON array with `newitem`. Use a non-negative index; negative returns `false`. It finds the existing element and delegates to `cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer`.
functions.cJSON_InsertItemInArray: Inserts `newitem` into `array` at index `which`. Use a nonnegative index and a non-NULL item. If `which` is past the end, it appends. Returns false on invalid args or corrupted array links.
functions.cJSON_PrintPreallocated: `cJSON_PrintPreallocated` renders a `cJSON` value into a caller-supplied buffer, avoiding internal allocation. Use it with a valid buffer and length; it returns 1 on success, 0 if `item` can’t fit, or if `buffer==NULL`/`length<0`. `format` controls pretty-printing.
functions.cJSON_AddTrueToObject: `cJSON_AddTrueToObject` creates a JSON `true` item and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it to set a boolean property. On success it returns the new item; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToObject: Adds `item` to a JSON object under key `string`. Use it with an object node and a cJSON item you want owned by that object. It returns `cJSON_bool` from the internal add helper; it’s the non-duplicating variant (uses the given string/item directly).
functions.cJSON_AddNumberToObject: Adds a numeric member to a JSON object. Use it with an existing `cJSON` object and key name; it creates a number item, inserts it, and returns that item on success. If insertion fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsFalse: `cJSON_IsFalse` checks whether a `cJSON*` is a JSON false literal. Use it to test an item’s type safely. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`, otherwise true only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_False`.
functions.cJSON_GetErrorPtr: `cJSON_GetErrorPtr()` is for diagnosing a failed `cJSON_Parse()`: it returns a pointer into the input at the parse error location. Use it only after parse failure; on success it returns `0`/NULL. You may need to inspect a few chars before it for context.
functions.cJSON_CreateString: Creates a new cJSON string item from a C string. Use it to build JSON values, not parse input. It allocates a cJSON node and duplicates `string`; on allocation failure it deletes the node and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_InitHooks: `cJSON_InitHooks` sets cJSON’s global memory hooks. Call it once before creating/parsing JSON to use custom `malloc/free` (and `realloc` only when both are default). Passing `NULL` resets to standard `malloc/free/realloc`.
functions.cJSON_PrintUnformatted: `cJSON_PrintUnformatted` serializes a `cJSON` item to compact JSON text with no spaces/newlines. Use it when you want transfer/storage-friendly output. It returns a newly allocated `char*` (or `NULL` on failure); free it with cJSON’s free hook.
functions.cJSON_AddArrayToObject: `cJSON_AddArrayToObject` creates a new empty JSON array and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it when you want to build nested JSON. On success it returns the new array; on failure it deletes it and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_IsTrue: `cJSON_IsTrue` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON boolean `true`. Use it on a `cJSON*`; it returns `false` for `NULL` and for any item whose base type isn’t `cJSON_True`.
functions.cJSON_GetNumberValue: `cJSON_GetNumberValue` returns a JSON number as `double`. Use it only on items that are numbers; otherwise it returns `NAN`. It’s a safe accessor that checks `cJSON_IsNumber(item)` before reading `valuedouble`.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringArray: Creates a JSON array of strings from `strings[0..count-1]`. Use with a non-NULL string pointer array and `count >= 0`. Returns NULL if args are invalid or any element creation fails; on failure it deletes the partially built array.
functions.cJSON_CreateIntArray: Creates a JSON array from `int` values. Use with a valid `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`; `count` must not exceed the source array length. Returns `NULL` on invalid args or allocation failure, otherwise a new array of number items.
functions.cJSON_AddNullToObject: Creates a JSON `null` item and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it to build objects in one step. Returns the added item on success, `NULL` on failure; on failure it deletes the created item.
functions.cJSON_SetNumberHelper: Helper for `cJSON_SetNumberValue`: set a cJSON number’s `valueint` with INT_MAX/INT_MIN clamping, then store `valuedouble`. Use it on a valid number item. Returns the assigned double.
functions.cJSON_Print: `cJSON_Print` renders a `cJSON` value into a newly allocated, formatted JSON text string using the global hooks. Use it to serialize an item for storage/transfer, then free the returned buffer with the matching cJSON free function. Returns `NULL` on failure.
functions.cJSON_IsString: `cJSON_IsString` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a string node. Use it to test an item before reading `valuestring`. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for any non-string type; otherwise `true` when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_String`.
functions.cJSON_AddObjectToObject: Creates a new empty JSON object and adds it to `object` under `name`. Use it to build nested objects. Returns the new child on success, or `NULL` if creation/addition fails; on failure the created item is deleted.
functions.cJSON_AddBoolToObject: Creates a JSON boolean item and adds it to an object under `name`. Use it for object members only. Returns the new item on success, `NULL` on failure; if insertion fails, the created item is deleted.
functions.cJSON_IsRaw: `cJSON_IsRaw` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a raw JSON value. Use it to test an item before treating it as `cJSON_Raw`. It returns `false` for `NULL`, otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_Raw`.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObject: `cJSON_DetachItemFromObject` finds the object member by key and detaches it from `object`, returning the removed `cJSON*`. Use it when you want to take ownership of a child without deleting it. If `object`/key is missing, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_Minify: `cJSON_Minify` is an in-place JSON cleaner: it removes whitespace and C-style comments from a writable `char *` buffer. Pass `NULL` to do nothing. Don’t use string literals/read-only memory, since it modifies the input.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemViaPointer: Replaces `item` in `parent` with `replacement` by pointer, preserving list links and shifting following items right. Use only when both nodes belong to `parent`. Returns false on NULL args; true if `replacement==item`; otherwise updates neighbors/child pointer.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Deletes a case-sensitive named child from a JSON object. Use it on an object and key string; it detaches the matching item, then frees it via `cJSON_Delete`. If no match exists, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_PrintBuffered: `cJSON_PrintBuffered` renders a cJSON item to text using an initial buffer guess to reduce reallocations. Use `prebuffer >= 0`; `fmt=0` unformatted, `fmt=1` pretty-printed. Returns allocated JSON text or `NULL` on bad size, alloc failure, or print failure.
functions.cJSON_AddItemToArray: `cJSON_AddItemToArray` appends a `cJSON` item to an array. Use it with an array node and an item node you want owned by that array. It returns `cJSON_bool` success/failure; it just forwards to `add_item_to_array`, so invalid args or allocation/linking failures can make it fail.
functions.cJSON_CreateArrayReference: Creates a cJSON array node that **references** an existing child list, not a copy. Use it when you want to wrap already-built items as an array without duplicating them. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`. The `cJSON_IsReference` flag means the child data isn’t owned here.
functions.cJSON_CreateNull: `cJSON_CreateNull()` allocates a new cJSON item and marks it as `cJSON_NULL`. Use it when you need a JSON `null` value in a tree. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`; otherwise you get a valid null item.
functions.cJSON_IsNull: `cJSON_IsNull` checks whether a `cJSON` item is the JSON `null` type. Use it on a `cJSON*` node. It returns `false` if `item == NULL`; otherwise `true` only when `(item->type & 0xFF) == cJSON_NULL`.
functions.cJSON_Compare: `cJSON_Compare` recursively checks whether two cJSON values are equal. Use it on valid `cJSON*`; `NULL`, invalid types, or mismatched base types return false. Same pointer returns true. For objects, `case_sensitive` controls key matching.
functions.cJSON_GetArraySize: `cJSON_GetArraySize` counts linked `child` nodes and returns the number of items in an array or object. Pass a valid `cJSON*`; if `array == NULL`, it returns 0. It iterates all children, so it’s O(n). Result is cast to `int` and may overflow for huge sizes.
functions.cJSON_HasObjectItem: `cJSON_HasObjectItem` is a convenience check for object members. Use it with a `cJSON` object and key string to test existence. It returns `1` if `cJSON_GetObjectItem` finds a matching item, otherwise `0`; it does not return the item itself.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObjectCaseSensitive: Replaces an object member by key using **case-sensitive** matching. Use it on a cJSON object with a key string and a new item; it returns `true` on success, `false` if the object/key is invalid or the member isn’t found.
functions.cJSON_IsBool: `cJSON_IsBool` checks whether a `cJSON` item is a boolean (`true` or `false`). Use it to test an item before reading it as a bool. It returns `false` for `NULL` and for non-bool types; otherwise `true` if either `cJSON_True` or `cJSON_False` flag is set.
functions.cJSON_AddStringToObject: Adds a JSON string member to an object. Use it with a valid `cJSON` object, key `name`, and C string `string`. It creates the string item, inserts it, returns the new item on success, or `NULL` on failure (and deletes the temp item).
functions.cJSON_DetachItemFromObjectCaseSensitive: Detaches and returns the child item from an object by exact key match. Use it when you want to remove an entry without deleting it. If object/key is missing, it returns `NULL`; the caller then owns the detached item.
functions.cJSON_ParseWithLengthOpts: Parses JSON from a buffer with an explicit length, avoiding reliance on `'\0'`. Use it when input may contain extra data or isn’t null-terminated. `return_parse_end` gets the stop position; if `require_null_terminated` is true, trailing non-space causes failure.
functions.cJSON_CreateArray:
Creates a new empty cJSON array node. Use it when you need an array container before adding elements. It allocates a new item; on success `type` is set to `cJSON_Array`, otherwise it returns `NULL`.
Yes, this is API misuse. Every successful cJSON_CreateArray() call returns a heap-allocated cJSON node whose ownership must later be released exactly once. If the created node is attached to another cJSON container via cJSON_AddItemToArray()/cJSON_AddItemToObject(), ownership transfers to that parent and you should delete only the root parent with cJSON_Delete(). If the node is detached with cJSON_DetachItemFromArray(), it becomes the caller’s responsibility again and must be freed with cJSON_Delete(). In this driver, array1 is the root and is never deleted, so the original tree leaks. To prevent future crashes/leaks: always call cJSON_Delete(array1) before returning; after cJSON_Duplicate(), free both the duplicate tree and the original tree; and on any early-return path, delete all successfully created root objects.
functions.cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject: `cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject` replaces an object member by key. Use it with a `cJSON` object, the target key string, and a new item. It returns `true` on success, `false` if the object/key is invalid or replacement fails.
functions.cJSON_DetachItemViaPointer: Detaches `item` from `parent`’s child list without deleting it. Use only with a valid child of `parent` (or `parent->child`). Returns the detached node, or `NULL` if `parent/item` is `NULL` or `item` isn’t in that list.
functions.cJSON_CreateFloatArray: Creates a JSON array from `float` values. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`; it returns `NULL` otherwise. On element creation failure, it deletes the partially built array and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_CreateRaw: `cJSON_CreateRaw` creates a `cJSON_Raw` item whose `valuestring` is a duplicated copy of `raw`. Use it to embed preformatted JSON text as-is. If allocation fails, it deletes the item and returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_GetArrayItem: `cJSON_GetArrayItem` returns the array element at `index`. Use it only with arrays and non-negative indices. If `index < 0`, it returns `NULL`; otherwise it delegates to internal lookup and returns `NULL` when the item can’t be found.
functions.cJSON_CreateObject: `cJSON_CreateObject()` allocates a new empty `cJSON` item and marks it as an object (`cJSON_Object`). Use it as the root or as a container, then add members with cJSON add APIs. If allocation fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.cJSON_AddItemReferenceToArray: Adds a reference node to an array, not a deep copy. Use it to reuse an existing `cJSON` item in another array without transferring ownership. Returns `false` if `array == NULL`; otherwise it wraps `item` via `create_reference()` and appends it.
functions.cJSON_SetValuestring: `cJSON_SetValuestring` updates the `valuestring` of a non-reference `cJSON_String` item. Use it only on valid string nodes with non-NULL current/new strings. It returns the stored string on success, or `NULL` if type/refs/NULL/corruption/overlap checks fail.
functions.cJSON_CreateStringReference: Creates a cJSON string node that **references** external memory, not owning it. Use it when the string lifetime is managed elsewhere. `cJSON_Delete` won’t free `valuestring`. Returns a new item or `NULL` on allocation failure.
functions.cJSON_free: `cJSON_free` is the library’s wrapper for freeing memory allocated by cJSON. Use it to release pointers returned/owned by cJSON, matching the allocator in `global_hooks`. It simply calls `global_hooks.deallocate(object)`; passing `NULL` is fine if the deallocator allows it.
functions.cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray: `cJSON_DeleteItemFromArray` removes the item at index `which` from a cJSON array and frees it. Use it when you want to delete an element in-place. It first detaches the item; if the index is invalid, nothing is deleted.
functions.cJSON_CreateDoubleArray: Creates a JSON array from a `double` C array. Use with a non-NULL `numbers` pointer and `count >= 0`. Returns `NULL` on invalid input or allocation failure; on success, each element is added as a JSON number, and partial arrays are deleted if creation fails.
